group: Sub‑schema found – segment is numeric and parent node is an array

cases.expected: Returns a JsonSchema instance whose schemaLocation and evaluationPath have been appended with index 0. No exception is thrown.
cases.description: The fragment points to the first element of an array. The method finds a non‑null subSchemaNode, recognises the segment as a Number while the current parent node is an array, updates schemaLocation/evaluationPath with the numeric index and creates a new sub‑schema because the resolved $id is either non‑null or this is the last segment.

group: Sub‑schema found – segment is a property name (object field)

cases.expected: Returns a JsonSchema instance whose schemaLocation/evaluationPath have been appended with the string "properties" then "name". No exception is thrown.
cases.description: The fragment points to a regular object property. The segment is not a Number, so the else‑branch updates the location with the segment’s string value and creates a sub‑schema because the $id is resolved (or it is the last segment).

group: Sub‑schema found – id is null and segment is not the last one

cases.expected: Returns the JsonSchema that corresponds to the last segment ("age"). The intermediate segment "person" does **not** cause a new sub‑schema creation because id == null and it is not the final segment.
cases.description: The method iterates over three segments. For the first segment ("definitions") id is null and x != nameCount‑1, therefore the inner `if ((id != null) || (x == nameCount‑1))` is false and `subSchema` remains null. When the last segment ("age") is processed, the condition becomes true because x == nameCount‑1, so a sub‑schema is finally created and returned.

group: Sub‑schema found – id is null but segment is the last one

cases.expected: Returns a JsonSchema instance for the node at "/singleLevel" even though the resolved id is null, because the segment is the last one.
cases.description: When the fragment consists of a single segment, the loop runs once (x == 0 == nameCount‑1). The condition `((id != null) || (x == nameCount‑1))` evaluates to true, forcing creation of the sub‑schema despite a null id.

group: Fragment not found – fetchSubSchemaNode returns null (exception path)

cases.expected: InvalidSchemaRefException is thrown with a ValidationMessage of type REF and code internal.unresolvedRef.
cases.description: The fragment cannot be resolved in the current document. `subSchemaNode` is null, `document.findSchemaResourceRoot().fetchSubSchemaNode` returns null, so the method throws an InvalidSchemaRefException.

group: Fragment not found – fetchSubSchemaNode returns a schema that can resolve the fragment

cases.expected: Returns the JsonSchema obtained from the recursive call `found.getSubSchema(fragment)`.
cases.description: When the fragment is not present in the current document, the method delegates to the root schema resource (`document.findSchemaResourceRoot().fetchSubSchemaNode`). That call returns a non‑null JsonSchema (`found`), which then successfully resolves the fragment via its own `getSubSchema` call, and the resulting sub‑schema is returned.

group: Intermediate sub‑schema created because $id is present

cases.expected: A JsonSchema instance is returned. After processing the first segment "components" the method resolves a non‑null $id in that node, creates a sub‑schema and updates schemaLocation/evaluationPath with "components". The second segment "schemas" is then processed on the new parent, again updating the locations. Finally the third segment "User" (with $id still non‑null) creates another sub‑schema, and the last segment "properties"/"id" are appended, resulting in a schema whose schemaLocation ends with "/components/schemas/User/properties/id" and evaluationPath mirrors it. No exception is thrown.
cases.description: The fragment has several segments. The node for the first segment contains a $id, so the condition `(id != null) || (x == nameCount‑1)` is true before the last segment, forcing early sub‑schema creation. The test verifies that early creation does not prevent later segments from being processed and that locations are correctly accumulated.

group: Numeric segment on a non‑array parent is treated as a string

cases.expected: A JsonSchema instance is returned. Although the segment is a Number (0), the current parent node is an OBJECT, so the method follows the else‑branch, appending the string "0" to schemaLocation and evaluationPath. No array‑specific index handling occurs.
cases.description: Ensures that numeric‑looking segments are only interpreted as array indexes when the parent node is actually an array. Here the parent is an object (the "properties" node), so the segment is handled like a normal property name.

cases.expected: null is returned (no sub‑schema created and no exception thrown).
cases.description: When the supplied JsonNodePath has `getNameCount() == 0`, the for‑loop is never entered. The method therefore returns the initially‑null `subSchema`. The test confirms that an empty fragment does not cause a NullPointerException or an exception.

group: Delegated schema resolves fragment but later fails – exception propagates

cases.expected: InvalidSchemaRefException is thrown. The initial document cannot resolve the fragment, `fetchSubSchemaNode` returns a non‑null JsonSchema (`found`), but `found.getSubSchema(fragment)` throws because the delegated schema also cannot resolve the fragment.
cases.description: Covers the path where the first document delegates to another schema resource, but that resource ultimately cannot resolve the fragment, leading to an exception bubbling up from the recursive call.

group: Multiple segments with mixed numeric and string handling

cases.expected: A JsonSchema instance is returned. The first segment "items" updates locations as a string. The second segment (numeric 0) is processed on an ARRAY node, causing numeric index handling (schemaLocation/evaluationPath append 0). The third segment "properties" and fourth "name" are appended as strings. The final schemaLocation ends with "/items/0/properties/name" and evaluationPath mirrors it.
cases.description: Validates that the method correctly switches between string and numeric handling as it traverses a path that includes an array index followed by object properties.

cases.expected: NullPointerException is thrown when the method attempts to call fragment.getNameCount() on a null reference.
cases.description: Passing a null JsonNodePath should result in an immediate NullPointerException because the implementation does not perform a null‑check before accessing fragment methods.

group: Root schema resource is null leading to NullPointerException

cases.expected: NullPointerException is thrown when the method tries to invoke methods on a null document returned by findSchemaResourceRoot().
cases.description: If findSchemaResourceRoot() is stubbed to return null, the subsequent call to document.getSchemaLocation() (or document.getEvaluationPath()) will cause a NullPointerException.

group: Parent schema node is null causing NullPointerException in getNode

cases.expected: NullPointerException is thrown when getNode(parentNode, segment) is invoked with parentNode == null.
cases.description: When the root schema's getSchemaNode() returns null (e.g., an empty or malformed schema), the loop will call getNode(null, segment) which leads to a NullPointerException inside the protected getNode implementation.

group: ValidationContext is null causing NullPointerException during $id resolution

cases.expected: NullPointerException is thrown when parent.getValidationContext() returns null and the code attempts to call resolveSchemaId(subSchemaNode).
cases.description: If the JsonSchema instance is constructed with a null ValidationContext, the call to parent.getValidationContext().resolveSchemaId(subSchemaNode) will dereference a null object, raising a NullPointerException.
